chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughters of the People of the Book, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem when they mention the Name of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, but I mean from them those who are upon the command of Musa and Isa (peace be upon them).'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: People of the Book (Jews and Christians)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the permissibility of eating the meat of the People of the Book according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits the meat of the People of the Book provided they invoke Allah's name, yet he refines this ruling by specifying that it applies to those who adhere to the Shari'ah of Musa and Isa, distinguishing them from others who may not follow these prophetic traditions. This nuance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the continuity of divine law and the specific theological status of the People of the Book within the framework of Tawhid. The condition highlights the importance of monotheistic intent and adherence to previous prophetic laws in determining the permissibility of their sacrifices.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, fromYunus, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughters of the People of the Book. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem when they mentioned the Name of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic, but I<sup>asws</sup> mean from them the ones who happen to be upon the commands of Musa<sup>as</sup> and Isa<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Isma’il ibn Marrar from Yunus from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the animals slaughtered by the people of the book. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful if they mention the name of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, and I mean those of them who are on the command of Moses and Jesus.’”
